note: A synthetic clause taxonomy for the example; it is not legal advice.

liability.what: Who bears a loss when something goes wrong, and how much of it
liability.not_for: Ending the agreement, or what is paid for the services
examples: Supplier's liability shall not exceed the fees paid

indemnity.what: One party covers the other's losses from claims brought by third parties
indemnity.not_for: A ceiling on damages, or kinds of loss excluded
examples: Each party shall defend and hold harmless the other against any third-party claim

mutual.not_for: Only one party gives an indemnity
examples: Each party shall indemnify the other against claims caused by its own breach

one_way.what: Only one party indemnifies the other
examples: Customer shall indemnify Supplier against any claim

limitation.what: A cap on damages, or kinds of loss that cannot be recovered
limitation.not_for: Covering claims brought by third parties
examples: In no event shall either party be liable for indirect damages

cap.what: The most a party can be liable for, as an amount or a multiple of fees
examples: Liability shall not exceed the fees paid in the prior twelve months

exclusion.what: Kinds of loss that cannot be recovered at all: indirect, consequential, lost profits
examples: Neither party is liable for loss of profits

termination.what: How and when the agreement ends
termination.not_for: What happens to confidential information after it ends
examples: Either party may terminate on thirty days' notice

convenience.what: Ending without giving a reason, on notice
convenience.not_for: Ending because the other party did something wrong
examples: Customer may terminate for convenience on thirty days' written notice

cause.what: Ending because the other party breached the agreement or became insolvent
examples: Either party may terminate if the other fails to cure a material breach

confidentiality.what: Keeping the other party's information secret
confidentiality.not_for: Personal data handled as part of the services
examples: Each party shall keep the other's Confidential Information secret

obligations.what: What must be kept secret, how, and for how long
examples: The obligations survive for three years after termination

exceptions.what: Information that is not confidential: public, already known, or required by law
exceptions.not_for: How long secrets must be kept
examples: This clause does not apply to information that is publicly available

payment.what: Fees, invoices, when they are due, and what happens when they are late
payment.not_for: Damages or refunds after something went wrong
examples: Customer shall pay each invoice within thirty days

terms.what: When invoices are issued and when they are due
terms.not_for: What happens when a payment is late
examples: Invoices are issued monthly in arrears and due in thirty days

late.what: Interest, fees or suspension when a payment is late
examples: Overdue amounts bear interest at one percent per month

general.what: Governing law, notices, assignment, entire agreement and other boilerplate
examples: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Oregon
